Welcome to this journey—one that invites us to pause and really think about the world we’re living in. Have you ever noticed how the clash between ancient faith and modern ideas can leave us feeling pulled in different directions? It’s a crossroads so many of us recognize, especially when we’re caught between what our hearts believe and what the world says is true.
There’s a powerful conversation waiting to unfold in Christina M. Lopez’s book, “Humanism: The Whore of Babylon and the Sleeping Church.” Here, we’ll explore the tension between humanism—where everything centers on human reason and autonomy—and the deep spiritual convictions that have guided generations before us.
What happens when the seductive pull of self-sufficiency and moral relativism begins to shape the very foundations of faith? Together, we’ll look at how human-centered thinking can subtly influence the spiritual health of the church, and why it matters so much to stay awake, alert, and discerning in a culture that often prizes individualism over divine truth.
Through vivid metaphors like the “Whore of Babylon,” representing deception and spiritual compromise, and the “Sleeping Church,” standing for believers who’ve drifted into complacency, Christina M. Lopez challenges us to reflect and ask: are we truly awake to what’s going on around us? Or have we allowed ourselves to grow indifferent?
So, let’s set out together to examine these urgent questions. Along the way, we’ll uncover what it means to hold fast to faith, stay vigilant, and answer the call to awaken in a world that’s always changing. There’s so much to discover—let’s begin.
